_comment: Every artifact sr-native links against or loads, pinned.
The rule this file exists to enforce: nothing floats. ncnn is pinned by tag AND
by commit AND by the SHA256 of the archive it was taken from, because a runtime
that changes underneath a release is not a runtime anyone can test against.
Model weights are never committed — they are downloaded and hash-checked.
`pwsh -File setup-third-party.ps1` rebuilds third_party/ and models/ from this
file. All hashes below were computed on the RTX 5070 Ti reference machine.

why_not_20250503: The RIFE models were exported against 20250503 — the commit the VapourSynth RIFE
fork's subprojects/ncnn resolves to — so that version was tested first, and it is
recorded here so nobody repeats it. ncnn 20250503 cannot submit to Vulkan on this
on the very first call, against an RTX 5070 Ti on driver 617.14. On the CPU it
produces the same result as 20260526, so it is not a semantics difference either.
It is not a usable pin on the reference machine.

tools.ncnnoptimize: converts the published fp16 weights to fp32 using ncnn's own reader

_comment: ncnn's Vulkan build needs a vulkan-1 import library. The Vulkan SDK supplies one,
along with glslangValidator; installing it needs elevation, which the reference
machine does not grant, so the import library is generated from the system loader
DLL instead. ncnn's release bundles glslang, so no shader compiler is needed.
Downloaded, never committed: .gitignore excludes models/. The published RIFE
weights are stored as fp16 and ncnn reads fp16 natively; the copy this runtime
loads is ncnnoptimize's fp32 conversion, whose hash is recorded separately.

installed._comment: what sr_rife_create loads: ncnnoptimize's fp32 output, plus its rewritten param

known_defect: The published artifact contains 288 fp16 words with exponent 31 (NaN/Inf).
This was verified against the published blob SHA, so the defect is in the
artifact rather than in the download or the conversion. Zeroing exactly those
words does not change the output by a measurable amount, so they are NOT the
cause of rife_pair_test failing; the artifact is kept byte-faithful.

rife-4.6.role: control — a second model, from a different repository, used to separate this harness from the 4.25 artifact
rife-4.6.result: fails identically in this harness — which is what cleared the 4.25 artifact as the cause

realesrgan-x4plus.verified: restore_image_test passes: luminance preserved, output differs from a bilinear upscale by 30.28 levels, tiled and untiled agree to 5.16 levels

reference_hardware.second_device: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics — integrated, unified memory, never eligible to host a model
reference_hardware.toolchain: Visual Studio 18 Community, MSVC 14.51.36231, CMake and Ninja from the same install
